newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar settles firmer, volume light.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar settles firmer, volume light.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended a thinly-traded session firmer and near the highs, lifted by speculative buying that carried May to its daily high just ahead of the close.
But the markt remained within its recent trading range in volume estimated at 7,276 lots. Friday's official volume was 7,365 lots.
Dealers said the market could remain rangebound until early to mid-April, when players begin to roll May positions into July and October.
Trade buying is expected to continue to support the market from 10.68 cents basis May, while speculative selling are likely to cap gains from 11.00 cents.
A dearth of fundamental news kept trade slim. Not even a cyclone, that hit Australia's sugarcane crop in the northern state of Queensland, inspired much movement.
Mike Palmerino, a meteorologist with Weather Services Corp, said the area was hit with between 8 to 12 inches of rain over the weekend, along with heavy winds.
"The wind may have been more of a factor than the rain. At 50 mph to 60 mph, it could have torn up some of the cane," he said.
May closed up 0.09 cent to 10.92 cents per lb, having traded from 10.94 to 10.83 cents. The outer contracts settled 0.09 to 0.06 higher.
Resistance in May remained at 11.05 cents and support at 10.68.
Open interest in most-active May fell 873 lots to 61,380 lots as of Friday's close.
